correctness.rationale: In a uniform pairing the probability of any prescribed loop is 1/(M-1); a prescribed pair of cross edges has probability 1/((M-1)(M-3)). Conditional on a marked loop, the remaining pairing is uniform and the corresponding a_i decreases by 2d_i-3. This derives E[L], E[P], E[LP] and the covariance formula. The D/2 expansion into pair, triple and degree-one terms is explicitly verified algebraically. The six-term AM–GM inequality makes each triple nonnegative with equality only at degrees (2,2,2); each negative (2,2) pair is outweighed by its distinct triple using a fixed degree-at-least-3 vertex. Parity handles degree-one vertices. The standalone verifier independently enumerated 63 small degree profiles and checked 4023 decomposition/sign profiles and 344 regular specializations; those finite checks are not treated as proof of the infinite range.

originality.rationale: The claimed new mathematical statement is the complete finite-size sign classification, not the standard model, indicators, marginal moments or asymptotic independent-Poisson property. Angel–van der Hofstad–Holmgren (2016) explicitly study the same L and P and compute their separate expectations (1.2),(1.6); their §3, especially (3.9), provides detailed signed-indicator overlap machinery used for asymptotic Poisson approximation, but no stated all-degree sign theorem. Janson (2006) §7 studies the sum of defects and Poisson convergence, not this sign classification. No direct statement or stronger theorem that yields the complete sign characterization without additional nontrivial inequality work was located in the inspected relevant portions. The ability to obtain the mixed moment by summing known elementary indicator probabilities is acknowledged; independent priority search remains prudent.

value.rationale: Self-loops and multiple-edge pairs are the canonical two defects of multigraph simplicity. Joint asymptotic Poisson approximation does not distinguish finite-size covariance signs. The universal irregular-degree classification isolates an exceptional positive two-regular phase, proves all other nondegenerate profiles negative, excludes accidental zeros, and supplies a proof certificate via degree-triple positivity. The regular limit exposes different orders of decay at degrees 2 and at least 3. This is a natural structural refinement, not a finite catalogue or parameter substitution.
